top.title: City slump again as Arsenal extend Premier League lead
top.description: Arsenal captain Martin Odegaard celebrates scoring against Hull at the Emirates Stadium (Henry Nicholls) Manchester City suffered a third consecutive Premier League defeat at the hands of Nottingham Forest on Saturday, allowing Arsenal to stretch their lead at the top of the table to six points. Enzo Maresca's men desperately needed a victory at the City Ground to keep pace with the in-form champions, who have taken 27 points from a possible 30, but lost 3-1. City had a mountain to climb after finding themselves 2-0 down in the 18th minute following goals from defender Jair Cunha and forward Liam Delap. The visitors were much improved after the break and Rayan Cherki cut the deficit with an emphatic strike into the roof of the net. But Delap restored Forest's two-goal advantage in the 73rd minute, rifling home with his left foot past the outstretched hand of Gianluigi Donnarumma to earn his side breathing room. Forest manager Oliver Glasner sprinted down the touchline to celebrate with his team, who had not managed to score a single Premier League goal at home before Saturday. City, who won their first seven league games under new manager Maresca, know that even if they close the gap to Arsenal, it might ultimately all be in vain. The Etihad club are still waiting to discover their fate after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules -- with a huge points deduction one potential punishment. - Odegaard strikes - Earlier, Arsenal made hard work of beating struggling Hull to underline their title credentials on the eve of the international break. Captain Martin Odegaard finally broke the deadlock for the champions and title favourites in the 72nd minute. Arsenal, who bossed possession at the Emirates, had a claim for a penalty in the closing minutes of the first half after Kai Havertz had his shirt pulled by Nobel Mendy. But VAR ruled that the German forward was in an offside position in the build-up. Frustration mounted as the second half unfolded but Odegaard came to Arsenal's rescue, scoring his first goal since early September with a poacher's finish. Noni Madueke cut in from the right before unleashing a left-footed shot that Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis spilled and Odegaard fired home from close range. Arsenal manager Arteta praised his players but wants them to be more clinical after they recorded a third 1-0 win in four league games. "We can still be much better, and we will improve in many phases, and we will get certain relationships to a different level that will be even more efficient," he said. "That's the next step, to have bigger margins and when we have them, the opportunities, put them away to make sure that we don't have to hang in there the last few minutes." top.title: Real Madrid scout 18-year-old English midfield talent wanted by Manchester United – report
top.description: Real Madrid scout 18-year-old English midfield talent wanted by Manchester United – report According to TeamTalk , Real Madrid have scouted Leicester City teenage midfielder Louis Page, who is being pursued by several top clubs in England, including Manchester United. The Red Devils already came close to signing the 18-year-old midfielder in the summer, but the move fell through. They continue to remain interested in the youngster but many other teams have now entered the fray. Real Madrid have watched Page According to the report, Real Madrid scouts have watched in action for Leicester City, with the club tracking more and more talents from England. The Merengues are already close to signing JJ Gabriel from Manchester United and seem to have identified Page as another prospect worth keeping an eye on. Louis Page is in demand. (Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images) The 18-year-old starlet is a product of the Leicester City youth academy and made his first-team breakthrough for the Foxes last season. So far in the current campaign, the Englishman has made 15 senior appearances, scoring one and assisting five goals. Page has a contract with Leicester until the summer of 2029, but the English club are open to a sale in January provided two conditions are met. Firstly, they want the youngster to remain at the club on loan for the remainder of the season, and secondly they are seeking a total fee of £15 million (€18 million) for their prized asset. Plenty of competition for Page As mentioned earlier, there is no shortage of interest in Page, with Manchester United understood to be the club pushing the hardest for his signing. Manchester United are confident of signing Page. (Photo by Alex Pantling/Getty Images) Meanwhile, Manchester City have also entered the race for the teenage midfielder, along with Chelsea and Arsenal. Other Premier League teams like Newcastle United, Aston Villa, and Brentford have also made enquiries. Outside of England, there has been interest from Borussia Dortmund, while Real Madrid’s arch-rivals, Barcelona have also watched him in action. For now, though, it is said that Manchester United remain confident of signing Page, who has six caps for the England U19 national team. Whether Real Madrid make a move for the teenager remains to be seen.

Drew Lock will make his second start this season, taking on the Arizona Cardinals once again. But the mystery of the elbow injury has now been solved, per Tom Pelissero. Seahawks QB Drew Lock has been battling severe tendinitis in his throwing elbow. But he looked good in limited practice reps and will start Sunday against Arizona in place of injured Sam Darnold, with free agency looming in March. More in The Sweep: https://t.co/2WjDotsn76 pic.twitter.com/shgYQc9NTO — Tom Pelissero (@TomPelissero) November 7, 2026 Lock’s availability was also somewhat in question this week, due to the tendinitis issue, but he apparently looked good enough in limited practice appearances to lead Seattle into a Week 9 divisional matchup. Lock made two appearances to start the season, posting a 127.3 passer rating (would lead the NFL if he had enough throws to qualify), 73% completion rate, 422 yards, 4 touchdowns and 0 interceptions. The hot start, coupled with turnover struggles from Sam Darnold, have had some fans clamoring to leave the backup inserted as the starter. A strained quad for Darnold will cause this idea to come to fruition for one week. The Arizona Cardinals defense has allowed the 2nd-most fantasy points to the QB position, so it will be interesting to see if big Lock lights it up again. Will the Seattle decision makers choose to ride the hot hand if the offense looks effective again, against a low-end opponent? Those are questions for another day. top.title: ‘I’d Have To Live With It’ — Todd McShay Identifies Scenario for NFL Teams To Draft Drew Mestemaker Over Jeremiah Smith
top.description: ‘I’d Have To Live With It’ — Todd McShay Identifies Scenario for NFL Teams To Draft Drew Mestemaker Over Jeremiah Smith The debate over the No. 1 overall pick in the 2027 NFL Draft could come down to a familiar question for NFL teams: Should they prioritize positional value or take the best player available? Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith is widely considered one of the top prospects in college football. However, NFL draft analyst Todd McShay believes there is a situation in which a team could pass on the talented receiver and select Oklahoma State quarterback Drew Mestemaker instead. For teams desperately searching for a franchise quarterback, that decision might be easier than it sounds. Drew Mestemaker Over Jeremiah Smith? McShay Explains Why During a discussion about the 2027 NFL Draft on “ The Triple Option” podcast , McShay was asked whether there was anyone in the class he would believe in enough to pass on Smith. The analyst pointed to Mestemaker, explaining, “We would have to have a plan organizationally, and I would have to have a strong belief in quarterback coach, but much more importantly, offensive coordinator slash head coach and in a developmental plan for Mestamaker, because we’re going to start him year one.” BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN’s Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator “I mean, that’s just how it works in the NFL. It’s just positional value. If we need one desperately, I’m not taking Jeremiah Smith over Mestamaker, and I’d have to live with it,” he added. McShay’s comments highlight the NFL’s emphasis on quarterbacks, as finding a franchise QB can change an organization’s future, even if Smith is the more talented prospect. Drew Mestemaker’s Rise Makes Him a Potential No. 1 Pick Mestemaker’s rise has been one of the more surprising stories in college football this season. The Oklahoma State quarterback was initially an unrated high school recruit and did not start a single varsity game at the position. He later walked on at North Texas before transferring to Oklahoma State for the 2026 season. Since arriving in Stillwater, Mestemaker has quickly climbed draft boards and established himself as one of the leading QB prospects in the 2027 class. A recent midseason poll of 25 NFL scouts and executives showed just how much his stock has increased. Seventeen of the 25 voters selected Mestemaker as their favorite to be the first quarterback taken in the draft. PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN’s Free NFL Playoff Predictor Entering Saturday’s game at Kansas State, Mestemaker had completed 184 of 281 passes for 2,649 yards, 25 touchdowns, and seven interceptions. Mestemaker also holds an 83.9 grade, ranking 28th on PFN’s CFB QB Impact Rankings . Other prospects who could enter the conversation for the No. 1 overall pick include Texas’ Colin Simmons and Arch Manning, Miami’s Darian Mensah, and South Carolina’s Dylan Stewart. top.title: Furious Tottenham set to cite Jean-Philippe Mateta's red card in formal complaint over Jayden Bogle's tackle at Leeds
top.description: Leeds United v Tottenham Hotspur - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Tottenham will lodge a formal complaint after Jayden Bogle escaped a red card for his reckless challenge on Mathys Tel in the 1-0 defeat at Leeds. Tel was forced off before half-time, and Spurs believe the decision clashes with Jean-Philippe Mateta's dismissal against them a week earlier, while Roberto De Zerbi insisted he still has full confidence in the officials. Tottenham to write to Pro Ref over Bogle decision Tottenham will submit a formal complaint to refereeing body Pro Ref after Bogle avoided a red card during Saturday's 1-0 defeat to Leeds at Elland Road. According to the Independent, Spurs believe the defender should have been sent off, and they will write to Pro Ref to seek an explanation as to why the incident did not result in a dismissal. Bogle lunged into a first-half tackle on Tel and landed on the forward's ankle with his left foot. Referee John Brooks awarded a foul to Spurs, but he did not show Bogle a card or punish him any further. VAR stays out as Tel is forced off Play was paused while Tel received treatment on the pitch, and VAR Tony Harrington looked at the incident in detail. After a four-minute review, Harrington decided against sending Brooks to the pitchside monitor, and although the challenge was deemed "reckless", Bogle went unpunished. Tel came back on, but he was replaced by Dominic Solanke after 43 minutes because of lingering effects on his Achilles. Leeds went on to win through a Noah Okafor goal, and speaking to the BBC, former Premier League assistant referee Darren Cann said: "Bogle's challenge meets the criteria for serious foul play as he endangers the safety of an opponent. He can consider himself lucky to still be on the pitch." Mateta red card could strengthen Spurs' case Spurs may cite the red card shown to Crystal Palace striker Mateta for his foul on Micky van de Ven in their 2-0 win a week earlier. On that occasion, referee Michael Oliver originally gave a yellow card, but it was upgraded after a VAR review. Later at Elland Road, Pedro Porro was booked for a challenge similar to Bogle's, which infuriated De Zerbi. De Zerbi was more critical of his own players after the game, but he said of the decision: "I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to the monitor. If they didn't take the right decision I don't know. We have to keep the eyes on the performance where can improve. I was surprised on the yellow card for Pedro Porro because it was clear. The potential red card, I couldn't say. We have full confidence in the referee and VAR. I cannot say nothing more." Key Match Incidents Panel to review Bogle tackle The Key Match Incidents Panel will review the decision in the coming days, while Tottenham await an explanation from Pro Ref. Mateta, meanwhile, is serving a three-match suspension after the Football Association rejected Palace's appeal against his red card.

top.description: KENNESAW, Georgia – Delaware ’s first football visit to Kennesaw State and Fifth Third Stadium holds reams of ramifications on Nov. 7. top.title: Mikel Arteta identifies two missing elements that can raise Arsenal’s level
top.description: After a familiar scoreline, Mikel Arteta has a new phrase. The Arsenal manager used some variation on “insist” several times throughout his press conference for the win over Hull City, after his team had almost been left standing at the door. Martin Odegaard instead offered a captain’s goal, for a third 1-0 win in four in the league. Like many of those, it could have been worse, but could have been better – especially in terms of finishing. Arsenal currently always feel one setback away from a big discussion about which forward they need to sign in January. They are obviously monitoring a few options, and are expected to do some business, but Arteta clearly doesn’t want his players thinking like that. He put it down to something else. When asked about what was actually a sixth win by one goal out of 10 Premier League games so far, he said they “need to be more efficient”. It could be argued that such a return is the height of efficiency, and that Arsenal could have been further ahead had they benefited from that debated penalty decision – but you know what he meant, especially with regard to finishing. Arteta lamented how his team had two further one-on-ones in the game, only to waste them. He said it was like they “are trying to score the perfect goal”. That’s another familiar refrain with this club, if from a different era to the 1-0s. Arteta’s desired solution is to be “more pragmatic”, that they “need to be more chaotic”. That’s undeniably true, but the manager being the one to say this poses some questions of his own. Another phrase that Arteta used was “volume”. That, when you face a defence as well structured as Hull City, you need to be “generating volume”. top.description: The anatomy of an upset: Fort Valley State beats Florida A&M in early season action appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Early-season basketball is usually treated as an afterthought, specifically in HBCU basketball. Out-of-conference games across the board often look lopsided, and the more compelling matchups don’t come until after the turn of the new year. But a couple of early-season matchups are often worth your attention, such as Jackson State’s compelling victory over Tulane on Thursday evening. Another game worth a spotlight was Fort Valley State University’s 75-70 victory over the Charlie Ward-led Florida A&M Rattlers . The game was particularly exciting for me as a Fort Valley State University alumnus, but I think it shows an interesting trend for both Fort Valley State as they head into SIAC competition and things that Florida A&M needs to clean up. A slow start, then a run It did not look like an upset for most of the first half. The Wildcats shot 11-of-35 from the field and 3-of-16 from three, and they went into halftime down 34-28 at the Al Lawson Center. FAMU, in turn, shot 44 percent and had led by as many as seven. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Then Fort Valley came out of the break on a 19-5 run. In the first six minutes of the second half the Wildcats went from down six to up eight, 47-39. Ronald Durham got it started with a layup off a steal, Inslee Carroll scored in the paint, and Ka’leel Stillman hit a three off a Carroll assist. Katayvon Jefferies then knocked down a three at the 15:31 mark to make it 40-39, and Fort Valley never trailed again. FAMU’s only points in that stretch were five from Jaden Kempson. Fort Valley made 16 of its 29 shots after the break (55.2 percent), including 5 of 9 from three, and hit 10 of 14 free throws. Fort Valley was the better team on Thursday night It might be odd to say that when a Division II program plays a Division I program, but Fort Valley State was clearly the better team throughout the game. They played with energy and aggressiveness FAMU wasn’t prepared for. The Wildcats forced 20 turnovers, 10 in each half, and finished with 13 steals. They scored 18 points off those turnovers to FAMU’s 14, and took 64 shots to FAMU’s 51. That is how they won, even though FAMU shot better at 47.1% to 42.2%. FAMU also won the rebounding battle 39-36, so Fort Valley created its edge through extra possessions. They also showed tremendous depth. Fort Valley’s bench scored 34 points to FAMU’s 15, and 23 of those came in the second half, when FAMU’s bench scored six. Jefferies, Stillman and Cordarius White accounted for all 34. Jefferies finished with 15 points on 5-of-12 shooting from three. Only one of the threes came in the first half, so 12 of his 15 points came after it. top.title: Nick Sirianni explains decision for Eagles QB change
top.description: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images The Eagles added Joe Milton to the roster just a few weeks ago, but he’s already getting an opportunity to turn things around for a struggling Philadelphia offense. Head coach Nick Sirianni spoke to reporters on Friday and explained their decision to promote Milton and demote Tanner McKee in the process. “Obviously, that’s always a difficult thing to think through because it isn’t ever just on one person. Matter of fact, I think Tanner [McKee] played solid, but this is just what I felt like we needed to do right at this particular moment to give ourselves the best chance to win this weekend.” Sirianni went on to say that Milton is talented and has been in Philly for a couple weeks, they’ve seen that he has a talented arm and is a talented athlete that can process and make decisions. “Just a lot of good qualities that [Joe Milton] has. I like his confidence and everything that he brings, and it’s been fun getting to know him and working with him.” The head coach also explained that they felt it was best to make the move now instead of waiting for the bye week, because they are doing everything they can to win each and every game. “At the end of the day, I have to make the decision based off of that. But every decision that we make, we talk through in great, great detail. Obviously, Howie [Roseman] and I talk in great detail, the offensive staff and I, Parks [Frazier] and Sean [Mannion] and everybody. We just talk through it. At the end of the day, my job as the head coach is to make these decisions that I think is best for the football team, but you discuss everything with everybody.” Sirianni was asked about comments on Monday in support of Tanner McKee keeping his job. He revealed that they were fresh off the Sunday night game, and that was the initial plan, but after looking through the film and planning for the next game, they went in another direction. He also confirmed that while they made a change at quarterback, they did not make any changes to coaches roles. The head coach talked about how they look at everything when evaluating players, including that McKee was leading an offense decimated by injuries. Still, he noted that everyone still has to the best with whatever their circumstances may be, but they evaluate everyone fairly. (INA FASSBENDER) Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund remain neck and neck at the top of the German Bundesliga table after 2-1 wins over Mainz and Elversberg on Saturday. Bayern and Dortmund, who drew 2-2 in Munich last Saturday, are locked on 21 points, with the defending champions ahead on goal difference after nine rounds. top.title: Inter clash will be major test of Como's level, says Fàbregas
top.description: FILE PHOTO - Como manager Cesc Fàbregas gestures on the touchline during the pre season friendly soccer match between Arsenal and Como 1907 at Emirates Stadium. (is associated with: «Inter clash will be major test of Como's level, says Fàbregas») John Walton/PA Wire/dpa Como boss Cesc Fàbregas says his side’s clash with Inter Milan will be a big test to see how much progress they have made. Second-placed Inter lost their unbeaten record in Serie A this season when they fell to a 3-1 defeat to derby rivals AC Milan last weekend and they will be looking to bounce back. Como are enjoying another impressive campaign themselves, sitting two places behind Inter, and are on a six-match winning run in all competitions, their latest victory a stunning 9-1 win away to Lens in the Champions League. Fàbregas told a press conference: “It feels like every week you ask me about a new test of our maturity. “We knew this season would be special for us, there is so much motivation, but we know our path. “This is an important match. We are coming off good form, but it is only a test to see where we can go. Inter remain the strongest team in Italy, we’ll see our level later.” Inter have proven Como’s bogey team since the latter were promoted in 2024. They have yet to beat Inter in the six meetings since their promotion, drawing only once in the first leg of a Coppa Italia semi-final and losing the rest. Fàbregas added: “We came close three times, but when Inter raise the bar, they become too strong for everyone. “We need to play our football, do our thing, without anxiety or pressure. After this match, we’ll see where we are. “I never stop learning from the best. The victory over Lens can happen once, if we’re lucky, in our lives, but Inter are the reigning champions of Italy, won the Coppa Italia, played two Champions League finals. “Who knows, tomorrow we might pull a surprise with the perfect performance.” Defeat to Milan saw Inter slip three points behind leaders Lazio. Inter captain Lautaro Martinez is unavailable for selection until after the international break through injury, while Luis Henrique is also out of the Como clash. However, Benjamin Pavard, John Stones and Curtis Jones have resumed training and could be in contention for Sunday’s game.

nigeria.description: Borussia Dortmund midfielder Jobe Bellingham said Saturday he hoped to fulfil a “huge dream” by playing alongside brother Jude after being called up to the England squad. On Friday, England manager Thomas Tuchel named Jobe, 21, in England’s 25-man squad for November’s Nations League fixtures with Croatia and Spain. Speaking after Dortmund’s 2-1 home win over Elversberg in the Bundesliga, Jobe said he and brother had acted out playing together for England when they were kids. “It’s really good. Olukoyede, who is also a senior pastor in the RCCG, made the disclosure while addressing church workers and ministers after the monthly Holy Ghost Service at the Redemption City of God, Simawa, Ogun State. The programme, held at the invitation of the General Overseer of RCCG, Pastor Enoch Adejare Adeboye, had as its theme, “Ethical Standard and Corruption in Christian Community.” Recounting the incident, the EFCC chairman said he had no option but to authorise the detention of the senior cleric because of the evidence available to the commission, stressing that the alleged misconduct did not involve the pastor’s activities in the church. “I say this with every sense of humility. It was a day that I had calls to detain a very senior pastor in this mission. I had no choice. I needed to do it because of what we have seen. “Not because of his activities, what he perpetrated within the church, no. But because of what happened in his place of work, where he works in his secular activities. I feel things like this should not be happening within the Christian community,” he said. Olukoyede warned church leaders against using the pulpit to promote materialism and questionable sources of wealth, saying the church must not give undue recognition to individuals suspected of involvement in financial crimes. He said churches should welcome everyone but must not celebrate or elevate people whose wealth was linked to criminal activities. “Some of us pervert holiness on our altars. We don’t preach as much holiness as we do of materialism. It must not be seen in our parishes giving front row to criminals. “We are not saying we should send them away, but we must not use the altar to promote financial fraudulent activities. nigeria.title: Rivers crisis: You’ll not regret choosing peace, Tinubu assures Fubara
nigeria.description: By Ayobami Okerinde President Bola Tinubu has assured Rivers State Governor, Siminalayi Fubara, that he would not regret his decision to embrace peace and respect the intervention of political elders in resolving the crisis that rocked the state. Tinubu gave the assurance on Saturday while addressing supporters at the All Progressives Congress, APC, 2027 presidential campaign rally in Port Harcourt. He said, “To me, I intervened on your behalf. Similarly, to Fubara, Your Excellency, the host governor of today, I want to thank you specifically for maturity, understanding, respect for the wisdom of elders. “When we intervened, you respected our position. You maintained peace. You are a committed democrat, Fubara. You will not regret what you have done as long as all of us are alive,” Tinubu said. The political crisis, which erupted in October 2023, followed a breakdown in relations between Fubara and his predecessor, now Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, over control of the state’s political structure. The crisis escalated in March 2025 when Tinubu declared a state of emergency in the state , suspending Fubara, his deputy, Ngozi Odu, and members of the House of Assembly for six months. Fubara returned to office in September 2025 following the expiration of the emergency rule. However, political tensions resurfaced, with lawmakers initiating another impeachment process against him and his deputy in January 2026. Efforts to reconcile the feuding camps gained momentum in June 2025 when Tinubu convened a meeting involving Fubara, Wike and members of the Rivers State House of Assembly at the Presidential Villa in Abuja. nigeria.title: Arsenal edge past Hull to stretch Premier League lead
nigeria.description: Arsenal beat stubborn Hull 1-0 to stretch their lead at the top of the Premier League to six points on Saturday while Tottenham’s recent revival was halted at Leeds. Mikel Arteta’s Gunners were strongly tipped to get the better of the visitors, who have not won in the league since August, but were made to sweat despite dominating the match. Captain Martin Odegaard finally broke the deadlock for the champions and title favourites in the 72nd minute to give Arsenal their ninth win in 10 games. Manchester City can close the gap to three points if they beat struggling Nottingham Forest in the late kick-off as they seek to avoid a third straight defeat. Arsenal, who hogged possession at the Emirates, had a claim for a penalty in the closing minutes of the first half after Kai Havertz had his shirt pulled by Nobel Mendy. But VAR ruled that Havertz was in an offside position in the build-up. Frustration mounted as the second half unfolded but Odegaard came to Arsenal’s rescue, scoring his first goal since early September with a poacher’s finish. Noni Madueke cut in from the right before unleashing a left-footed shot that Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis spilled, with Odegaard firing home from close range. – VAR controversy – In the early kick-off, Leeds struck in the 79th minute through substitute Noah Okafor to end Tottenham’s three-match winning run. The major talking point in the first half was a challenge by Leeds defender Jayden Bogle on Spurs winger Mathys Tel, which was reviewed for a potential red card by VAR officials before eventually being cleared. Tel had to leave the field shortly before half-time. Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi, disappointed by his team’s second-half showing, refused to be drawn on the incident, which was not reviewed on the pitchside monitor by referee John Brooks. “In the first situation of Mathys Tel I didn’t see, I can’t say nothing,” he told TNT Sports after the 1-0 defeat. He added: “I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to watch the clip or not. I think there was the VAR and if they didn’t take the right decision, I don’t know, but we have confidence.” Defeat is a bitter blow for Spurs, who arrived at Elland Road in buoyant mood after recovering from a shocking start to the season. Leeds manager Daniel Farke said his team, who had been winless in five league games, had shown “great spirit, great commitment, great unity”. Elsewhere, Jacob Murphy put Newcastle on course for a much-needed win with a spectacular strike in the 80th minute at Craven Cottage but substitute Rodrigo Muniz levelled just three minutes later to earn a 1-1 draw. entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. sports.description: Liam Delap scored twice as Nottingham Forest beat Manchester City (Darren Staples) Manchester City slumped to a third consecutive Premier League defeat on Saturday as Liam Delap's double lifted Nottingham Forest out of the relegation zone with a 3-1 win at the City Ground. Oliver Glasner's men had not scored at home at all this season, but pounced on City's defensive errors to strike twice in the first 20 minutes through Jair Cunha and Delap. Rayan Cherki's stunning strike gave City hope, but their title challenge is rapidly wilting even before the potential effects of a major points deduction. Delap sealed just Forest's second win of the season with an incredible strike in off the post on the night that could launch his career for the two-time European champions, after a difficult start since his club-record £50 million ($67 million) move from Chelsea. Defeat leaves City six points adrift of leaders Arsenal and with questions over whether the uncertainty surrounding the club is playing a part in their on-field slump. Found guilty on over 100 Premier League charges of breaking financial rules, the 10-time English champions face a severe points penalty unless they can overturn that verdict on appeal. Glasner warned his players he would make big changes after a disappointing start to his reign saw them start the match in the bottom three. sports.title: Furious Tottenham set to cite Jean-Philippe Mateta's red card in formal complaint over Jayden Bogle's tackle at Leeds
sports.description: Leeds United v Tottenham Hotspur - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Tottenham will lodge a formal complaint after Jayden Bogle escaped a red card for his reckless challenge on Mathys Tel in the 1-0 defeat at Leeds. Tel was forced off before half-time, and Spurs believe the decision clashes with Jean-Philippe Mateta's dismissal against them a week earlier, while Roberto De Zerbi insisted he still has full confidence in the officials. Tottenham to write to Pro Ref over Bogle decision Tottenham will submit a formal complaint to refereeing body Pro Ref after Bogle avoided a red card during Saturday's 1-0 defeat to Leeds at Elland Road. According to the Independent, Spurs believe the defender should have been sent off, and they will write to Pro Ref to seek an explanation as to why the incident did not result in a dismissal. Bogle lunged into a first-half tackle on Tel and landed on the forward's ankle with his left foot. Referee John Brooks awarded a foul to Spurs, but he did not show Bogle a card or punish him any further. VAR stays out as Tel is forced off Play was paused while Tel received treatment on the pitch, and VAR Tony Harrington looked at the incident in detail. After a four-minute review, Harrington decided against sending Brooks to the pitchside monitor, and although the challenge was deemed "reckless", Bogle went unpunished. Tel came back on, but he was replaced by Dominic Solanke after 43 minutes because of lingering effects on his Achilles. Leeds went on to win through a Noah Okafor goal, and speaking to the BBC, former Premier League assistant referee Darren Cann said: "Bogle's challenge meets the criteria for serious foul play as he endangers the safety of an opponent. He can consider himself lucky to still be on the pitch." Mateta red card could strengthen Spurs' case Spurs may cite the red card shown to Crystal Palace striker Mateta for his foul on Micky van de Ven in their 2-0 win a week earlier. On that occasion, referee Michael Oliver originally gave a yellow card, but it was upgraded after a VAR review. Later at Elland Road, Pedro Porro was booked for a challenge similar to Bogle's, which infuriated De Zerbi. De Zerbi was more critical of his own players after the game, but he said of the decision: "I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to the monitor. If they didn't take the right decision I don't know. We have to keep the eyes on the performance where can improve. I was surprised on the yellow card for Pedro Porro because it was clear. The potential red card, I couldn't say. We have full confidence in the referee and VAR. I cannot say nothing more." Key Match Incidents Panel to review Bogle tackle The Key Match Incidents Panel will review the decision in the coming days, while Tottenham await an explanation from Pro Ref. Mateta, meanwhile, is serving a three-match suspension after the Football Association rejected Palace's appeal against his red card.

sports.description: After a familiar scoreline, Mikel Arteta has a new phrase. The Arsenal manager used some variation on “insist” several times throughout his press conference for the win over Hull City, after his team had almost been left standing at the door. Martin Odegaard instead offered a captain’s goal, for a third 1-0 win in four in the league. Like many of those, it could have been worse, but could have been better – especially in terms of finishing. Arsenal currently always feel one setback away from a big discussion about which forward they need to sign in January. They are obviously monitoring a few options, and are expected to do some business, but Arteta clearly doesn’t want his players thinking like that. He put it down to something else. When asked about what was actually a sixth win by one goal out of 10 Premier League games so far, he said they “need to be more efficient”. It could be argued that such a return is the height of efficiency, and that Arsenal could have been further ahead had they benefited from that debated penalty decision – but you know what he meant, especially with regard to finishing. Arteta lamented how his team had two further one-on-ones in the game, only to waste them. He said it was like they “are trying to score the perfect goal”. That’s another familiar refrain with this club, if from a different era to the 1-0s. Arteta’s desired solution is to be “more pragmatic”, that they “need to be more chaotic”. That’s undeniably true, but the manager being the one to say this poses some questions of his own. Another phrase that Arteta used was “volume”. That, when you face a defence as well structured as Hull City, you need to be “generating volume”. In other words, numbers, a critical mass of chances where you eventually score – which is pretty much what they did. Insistence. Martin Odegaard took advantage inside the box to earn Arsenal a slender win (PA) It’s been discussed on these pages before that Arteta is a huge “probabilities guy”, where he sees almost every game as an equation. If Arsenal consistently generate an xG of 2 or above and limit the opposition to 0.5, they are likely to win enough games to win the league. sports.description: The anatomy of an upset: Fort Valley State beats Florida A&M in early season action appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Early-season basketball is usually treated as an afterthought, specifically in HBCU basketball. Out-of-conference games across the board often look lopsided, and the more compelling matchups don’t come until after the turn of the new year. But a couple of early-season matchups are often worth your attention, such as Jackson State’s compelling victory over Tulane on Thursday evening. Another game worth a spotlight was Fort Valley State University’s 75-70 victory over the Charlie Ward-led Florida A&M Rattlers . The game was particularly exciting for me as a Fort Valley State University alumnus, but I think it shows an interesting trend for both Fort Valley State as they head into SIAC competition and things that Florida A&M needs to clean up. A slow start, then a run It did not look like an upset for most of the first half. The Wildcats shot 11-of-35 from the field and 3-of-16 from three, and they went into halftime down 34-28 at the Al Lawson Center. FAMU, in turn, shot 44 percent and had led by as many as seven. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Then Fort Valley came out of the break on a 19-5 run. In the first six minutes of the second half the Wildcats went from down six to up eight, 47-39. Ronald Durham got it started with a layup off a steal, Inslee Carroll scored in the paint, and Ka’leel Stillman hit a three off a Carroll assist. Katayvon Jefferies then knocked down a three at the 15:31 mark to make it 40-39, and Fort Valley never trailed again. FAMU’s only points in that stretch were five from Jaden Kempson. Fort Valley made 16 of its 29 shots after the break (55.2 percent), including 5 of 9 from three, and hit 10 of 14 free throws. Fort Valley was the better team on Thursday night It might be odd to say that when a Division II program plays a Division I program, but Fort Valley State was clearly the better team throughout the game. They played with energy and aggressiveness FAMU wasn’t prepared for. The Wildcats forced 20 turnovers, 10 in each half, and finished with 13 steals. They scored 18 points off those turnovers to FAMU’s 14, and took 64 shots to FAMU’s 51. That is how they won, even though FAMU shot better at 47.1% to 42.2%. FAMU also won the rebounding battle 39-36, so Fort Valley created its edge through extra possessions. They also showed tremendous depth. Fort Valley’s bench scored 34 points to FAMU’s 15, and 23 of those came in the second half, when FAMU’s bench scored six. Jefferies, Stillman and Cordarius White accounted for all 34. Jefferies finished with 15 points on 5-of-12 shooting from three. Only one of the threes came in the first half, so 12 of his 15 points came after it. Two of them came 39 seconds apart and pushed a 53-48 lead to 59-48. Stillman added 11 points, and White scored eight on 4-of-5 shooting. No need to panic at Florida

sports.title: Nick Sirianni explains decision for Eagles QB change
sports.description: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images | Getty Images The Eagles added Joe Milton to the roster just a few weeks ago, but he’s already getting an opportunity to turn things around for a struggling Philadelphia offense. Head coach Nick Sirianni spoke to reporters on Friday and explained their decision to promote Milton and demote Tanner McKee in the process. “Obviously, that’s always a difficult thing to think through because it isn’t ever just on one person. Matter of fact, I think Tanner [McKee] played solid, but this is just what I felt like we needed to do right at this particular moment to give ourselves the best chance to win this weekend.” Sirianni went on to say that Milton is talented and has been in Philly for a couple weeks, they’ve seen that he has a talented arm and is a talented athlete that can process and make decisions. “Just a lot of good qualities that [Joe Milton] has. I like his confidence and everything that he brings, and it’s been fun getting to know him and working with him.” The head coach also explained that they felt it was best to make the move now instead of waiting for the bye week, because they are doing everything they can to win each and every game. “At the end of the day, I have to make the decision based off of that. But every decision that we make, we talk through in great, great detail. Obviously, Howie [Roseman] and I talk in great detail, the offensive staff and I, Parks [Frazier] and Sean [Mannion] and everybody. We just talk through it. At the end of the day, my job as the head coach is to make these decisions that I think is best for the football team, but you discuss everything with everybody.” Sirianni was asked about comments on Monday in support of Tanner McKee keeping his job. He revealed that they were fresh off the Sunday night game, and that was the initial plan, but after looking through the film and planning for the next game, they went in another direction. He also confirmed that while they made a change at quarterback, they did not make any changes to coaches roles. The head coach talked about how they look at everything when evaluating players, including that McKee was leading an offense decimated by injuries. Still, he noted that everyone still has to the best with whatever their circumstances may be, but they evaluate everyone fairly. Second-placed Inter lost their unbeaten record in Serie A this season when they fell to a 3-1 defeat to derby rivals AC Milan last weekend and they will be looking to bounce back. Como are enjoying another impressive campaign themselves, sitting two places behind Inter, and are on a six-match winning run in all competitions, their latest victory a stunning 9-1 win away to Lens in the Champions League. Fàbregas told a press conference: “It feels like every week you ask me about a new test of our maturity. “We knew this season would be special for us, there is so much motivation, but we know our path. “This is an important match. We are coming off good form, but it is only a test to see where we can go. Inter remain the strongest team in Italy, we’ll see our level later.” Inter have proven Como’s bogey team since the latter were promoted in 2024. They have yet to beat Inter in the six meetings since their promotion, drawing only once in the first leg of a Coppa Italia semi-final and losing the rest. Fàbregas added: “We came close three times, but when Inter raise the bar, they become too strong for everyone. “We need to play our football, do our thing, without anxiety or pressure. After this match, we’ll see where we are. “I never stop learning from the best. The victory over Lens can happen once, if we’re lucky, in our lives, but Inter are the reigning champions of Italy, won the Coppa Italia, played two Champions League finals. “Who knows, tomorrow we might pull a surprise with the perfect performance.” Defeat to Milan saw Inter slip three points behind leaders Lazio. It’s a team with a real spirit, and we can build a great deal on that. We’re enjoying a good run of positive results, but we want to keep improving in terms of our style of play as well. In the second half, we upped the tempo, moving the ball around more quickly and making better use of switches of play against a side that tended to sit deep. The girls did well to read the game and, above all, never gave up. Even after going 2–1 up, we kept pushing for a third goal, which shows the mentality of the squad. We now face a very busy period, with five matches in fifteen days. We’ll be facing one of the strongest teams in the world, but we have great confidence in our chances. With this spirit, we can compete against anyone. We’ll try to recover our energy as quickly as possible so that we’re ready.” CECILIA SALVAI “We conceded a goal that we could have avoided, and that made the match a bit more difficult, but we were aware of our strength. We had to be patient, keep believing in what we were doing, and in the end we managed to turn the game around. I’m happy about the goal, but above all about the win, because it was the result of great teamwork. Wednesday’s match against Lyon will be a completely different affair, we’re up against the most successful team in Europe in the Champions League, and we’ll have to pay close attention to every detail. However, we’re playing at home, we’re full of confidence and we’re in good form. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
science.description: null On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected. But a space maneuver accidentally exposed one of its batteries to the sun, and the spacecraft lost power. It fell silent forever in November 2006 . NASA launches the Mars Global Surveyor to Mars on a Delta II rocket on Nov. 7, 1996. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered As the first successful Mars mission since the two Viking launches in 1975, Mars Global Surveyor ushered in a new era of exploration of the Red Planet, not only through its own contributions to orbit-based science, but by serving a relay for surface-based rovers. As such, it became a primary pipeline for multiple concurrent Mars missions. "The [Mars Global Surveyor] mission overhauled scientists' understanding of Mars by studying the entire Martian surface, atmosphere and interior. Major findings included dramatic evidence that water still flows on Mars in short bursts down hillside gullies, and the identification of water-related mineral deposits leading to selection of a Mars rover landing site for a subsequent mission," read a NASA description of the probe. Mars Global Surveyor sent back more than 240,000 images to Earth during its nine active years. Want more space history? science.description: null We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034. "Nearly a billion miles away, an extraordinary destination awaits. Titan has an atmosphere, rivers and lakes, seasons, sweeping dunes and a landscape rich in organic material," NASA officials wrote in the event page. "Upon arrival in 2034, Dragonfly will fly from place to place on this intriguing world to uncover clues about this remarkable moon, and the chemistry that could help us understand the ingredients for life." Dragonfly will be one of just a few flying crafts on another world, with the first being NASA's plucky Ingenuity mini-helicopter that arrived on Mars along with the still-running Perseverance rover in 2021. Ingenuity was only designed to make five flights, but made it to 72 until its blades were damaged during a landing on Jan. 18, 2024. NASA is now planning a SkyFall mission on Mars that would use three helicopters, and which may launch as soon as late 2028 for the Red Planet. Dragonfly, however, is not the first mission to Titan: that would be Huygens , which operated for just a few hours on Jan. 14, 2005 after deploying from the Cassini spacecraft. Huygens was the first lander on an outer solar system world, and measured Titan's atmosphere and took data from the surface. A mosaic image of Saturn's moon Titan composed of images produced by the Cassini spacecraft. (Image credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona/University of Idaho) For its part, Cassini flew by Titan more than 100 times before the mission concluded in September 2017 , providing valuable long-term data about the moon from above. Dragonfly aims to show the moon from up close for about 3.3 Earth years. Its destinations will include dunes and a young impact crater called Selk, according to NASA. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 6, 1572: A German astronomer discovers the Tycho supernova with the naked eye, but everyone thought the cosmic explosion was a 'new star'
science.description: null On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day. Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star." At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago. Because Tycho's Star is 13,000 light-years from Earth, it took a while before anyone could see it. The Tycho supernova remnant as seen by the Chandra X-ray space telescope. (Image credit: X-ray: NASA/CXC/RIKEN & GSFC/T. Sato et al; Optical: DSS) Why it mattered The Tycho supernova, known technically as SN 1572 , is known today as a Type Ia supernova, which is a star explosion in a binary star system in which a white dwarf star draws material away from its partner, then explodes. But in 1572, the Tycho supernova appeared as something very different: a bright new star. While Schulër was first, other astronomers also observed the apparently new star in the sky. Tycho Brahe's numerous observations are the most well known, in no small part becuause he wrote a book all about them in "De Stella Nova" (Latin for "On The New Star." At the time, the prevailing theory among scientists was that the stars were unchanging, yet here was a new star -- a changed sky. "The 16th century exploding star, which appeared in the constellation Cassiopeia , was seen in daylight for about two weeks, and remained visible to the naked eye for 16 months," the University of California Berkeley wrote in 2004 . "Brahe's meticulous record of the brightening and dimming of the supernova now allows astronomers to identify its 'light signature" as that of a Type Ia supernova." "This was at the end of the Dark Ages in Europe, and these observations were an important piece of evidence that the heavens were not immutable," astronomer Alex Filippenko, who led a 2004 study on the origins of the Tycho supernova, said at the time . Today, astronomers are closely watching another star that might explode. Called T Corona Borealis , or the Blaze Star , the object is expected to be on the verge of exploding in a nova (a star explosion that is smaller than a supernova and may not destroy the star). is one of 11 known stars observed to have recurring nova explosions within gaps of 100 years or so. science.title: What's that bright 'star' in the early morning sky? It's not a star at all!
science.description: null Early morning risers heading to work or school before sunrise are likely to notice a very bright, star-like object appearing low in the east-southeast sky just before sunrise. What is somewhat amazing is that just a couple of weeks ago this object wasn't there at all, but now it literally stands out with such brilliance as to almost command the attention of commuters who might be traveling in an easterly direction to "Look at me!" The object in question is, of course, the planet Venus, which is currently amid one of its most spectacular forays into the morning sky, literally "vaulting up" into prominence. On Oct. 24, Venus came to inferior conjunction, passing between the Earth and sun and shifting from the evening into the morning sky. And the view is only going to get better in the days and weeks to come! Ascending in the morning In terms of morning visibility, Venus is now in a literal and figurative sense "rising to the occasion." It's now rising before the break of dawn, more than 90 minutes before sunrise. From here on, it will rise three minutes earlier each day, so that by Dec. 17 it will rise 3 hours and 50 minutes before sunrise and blaze in a completely dark sky for more than two hours before the first vestige of morning twilight. It will reach peak brilliance on Nov. 29, when it will shine at an eye-popping magnitude of -4.9. That's 12 times brighter than its nearest planetary competitor, Jupiter and a full 25 times more dazzling than Sirius, the brightest of all stars. If you live in a rural location with no light pollution to interfere, you might be able to make out that it is casting a visible shadow and if you follow it right on through sunrise, it will be evident to your naked eye in full daylight: a tiny white speck plainly evident against the blue daytime sky. In a way, we could even regard Venus as this year's version of a "Christmas Star," glowing with stunning radiance ". . . in the east" like the biblical quote mentioned in St. Matthew. What goes up, must come down After reaching its high point in terms of morning visibility in mid-December, Venus will start a long, slow slide back toward the sun, rising about 1½ minutes later each morning from New Year's Day through late March. By then, Venus will be coming up as dawn is breaking, roughly 100 minutes before sunrise. Venus will continue to get gradually lower and rise progressively later during the spring and by late June it will be coming up less than an hour before sunrise, ultimately vanishing into the bright dawn twilight by July. Venus will then go on a "summer sabbatical" of sorts and will not reappear again until about this time next year when it will begin a very fine evening apparition. So, if any of your friends or relatives remark to you that they saw a "strange UFO" on the way to work or school recently, you now can set them straight. It's not E.T. It's only Venus. science.title: Record-breaking, fast-spinning magnet could help uncover new physics
science.description: Magnets can be made to levitate by the Meissner effect Science History Images / Alamy A tiny magnet that levitates within a superconductor trap may be the fastest spinning object visible to the naked eye, and one of the fastest spinning objects ever made. In the future, it could be used in experiments searching for mysterious dark matter particles and aid the development of quantum technologies. Superconductors are materials that conduct electricity with perfect efficiency, and they also expel any magnetic field that tries to permeate them – a phenomenon known as the Meissner effect. Because of this, a magnet placed above a superconductor experiences repulsive magnetic forces and starts to levitate. Tao Wang at the Agency for Science Technology and Research in Singapore and his colleagues have now set one such levitating magnet spinning at an unprecedently fast rate. Read more A miniature magnet rivals behemoths in strength for the first time The researchers used a spherical magnet made from neodymium, iron and boron that was about 30 micrometres wide, similar to the width of a fine human hair. They placed it in a cylindrical container made from lead, then enclosed that container in a chamber devoid of air, or a vacuum chamber. Advertisement Next, they used liquid helium to cool the whole setup to approximately -269°C (-452°F), only a few degrees above the coldest possible temperature . Under these extreme circumstances, lead behaved as a superconductor and the lack of air meant that the magnet could levitate within it without bumping into any particles. The team set the magnet spinning with a magnetic coil, ultimately pushing this tiny rotor to 138 million revolutions per minute. Wang says the magnet’s spinning was also very stable: it would take 17 days for its spinning speed to decrease by 50 per cent, something that would typically happen more quickly due to interactions between the magnet and its environment. “In terms of how many turns it makes before slowing down significantly, this is in the same league as the Earth’s spinning,” he says. “This, so far, is the fastest magnetically levitated rotor.” The record for the fastest rotating human-made object is also held by a levitated sphere, but that one was nano-sized, so invisible to the naked eye, and levitated by laser beams. Read more Physics of light and magnetism rewritten after almost two centuries Because the rotor experiences essentially no friction, and it is magnetic and cold, its behaviour is very sensitive to its environment, which makes it a promising sensor. The team has already successfully tested it as a gauge of vacuum at very low temperatures. Wang says this could be useful for builders of quantum computers, which often must be kept extremely cold and isolated in order to work. Benjamin Stickler at Ulm University in Germany says the levitated spinning magnet could also be used to precisely sense and measure magnetic fields. science.title: An unexpected feedback loop may be driving mega heatwaves
science.description: Land scorched by a fire in Wennington, London, during the record-breaking heatwave in 2022 Shutterstock Mid-latitude regions such as Europe are set to suffer more intense heatwaves than previously thought, according to new research that has uncovered a three-way feedback loop that amplifies extreme heat conditions. Heatwaves across the world have shocked scientists with their scale and severity in recent years, with heat extremes dramatically outstripping both historical records and the predictions of climate models. Read more Extreme heat is now making cities unlivable. How can we survive it? In the UK in 2022, temperatures exceeded 40°C (104 ° F) for the first time in history, despite predictions that such a milestone was probably still years away. Likewise, the 2021 heatwave in the Pacific Northwest saw temperatures hit extremes that far outstripped climate model projections. Advertisement Researchers have been scrambling to understand why very extreme heat is occurring more frequently, and with greater intensity, than expected at this level of warming. One team thinks the answer lies partly in the soil. Scientists already knew that high-pressure systems allow more solar radiation to reach Earth’s surface, heating up the land. They also knew that higher temperatures dry soils more quickly, removing the cooling effect provided by evaporation, thereby further amplifying heatwaves. Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter Now it seems that when temperatures climb high enough, dry soil, high pressure and extreme heat can amplify each other further, with dry soil helping to sustain high-pressure systems in the atmosphere. “Basically, the soils that are affected by circulation pattern also start to affect back on the circulation pattern itself,” says Kai Kornhuber at the International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis in Austria. This three-way feedback effect makes extreme heatwaves 10 per cent hotter than they would otherwise be, according to the research by Kornhuber and his colleagues – a factor not fully accounted for in climate model projections. This will have serious consequences for our ability to cope with future extreme heat. “Ten per cent hotter or colder can really make a difference between a heatwave and a record-shattering heatwave,” says Kornhuber. “We’re facing so many critical thresholds in social and biophysical systems that an extra 10 per cent can really lead to temperatures that are then quite damaging.” Read more Is a broken jet stream causing extreme weather that lasts longer? This may include serious public health consequences, a breakdown of vital infrastructure such as transport links and energy grids, crop failures and the collapse of ecosystems. science.title: You can see another galaxy with the naked eye — here's how to find it
science.description: null The first time I showed someone the Andromeda galaxy (M31), our conversation did not go quite as planned. I'd carefully worked my way across the sky, starting from the Great Square of Pegasus and hopping from star to star until I was confident I had the right patch. I pointed the telescope, got M31 in its crosshairs and proudly announced to my wife that I had found the closest giant galaxy to the Milky Way . Would she like to see it? She then stayed quiet for a little too long as she looked through the eyepiece. Then came an unexpected question. "Is it near that little smudge?" Hmmm. "Err, no. It is that little smudge," I replied. There was a pause. Of course, I knew exactly what had happened. We'd both seen photographs of M31 — a vast spiral galaxy with a brilliant center, sweeping dust lanes and hundreds of billions of stars. What we were actually looking at was a grayish blur that could easily have been mistaken for a mark on the eyepiece. That apparent disappointment is now my favorite part of finding Andromeda because the unimpressive smudge is real. The light entering your eyes has been traveling across space for about 2.5 million years. No screen, photograph or telescope is necessary. You are intercepting ancient light in your backyard. Technically, the Triangulum Galaxy (M33), about 2.7 million light-years away, can be seen with the naked eye, so it is therefore the most distant object the naked eye can see. But not mine — I've never seen it. M31 is a much more realistic naked-eye target. What's happening and when to look The Andromeda galaxy is at its most dramatic in photographs, not an eyepiece. (Image credit: Created using Canva and a base image from Starry Night) Early November is an excellent time to find M31 from the Northern Hemisphere. It's high and well placed during the evening, and this week the moon is becoming particularly cooperative. New Moon falls around Nov. 9, giving us several evenings with little or no moonlight to wash out faint deep-sky objects. I usually begin with the star Alpheratz, one of the corner stars of the Great Square of Pegasus. You go two stars left, two stars up, and you arrive at M31. Another route — and a good way to check you're in the right place — starts in Cassiopeia, the distinctive W-shaped constellation high in the northeastern sky on autumn evenings. You can use its second V-shape as an arrow pointing straight at M31. You can do that star-hop with the naked eye or a pair of binoculars, but M31 is visible to the naked eye only under a very dark sky. However, don't look for a miniature version of the photographs. Expect a faint, elongated patch with a slightly brighter middle. There's another beginner trap to avoid. Images make Andromeda look compact, but its full apparent extent is enormous — several times the width of the full moon — and our eyes usually pick up only the much brighter central region. science.title: Giant exoplanet emerges from the dark when the James Webb Space Telescope turns out the starlight
science.description: null Sometimes science can seem really counter-intuitive. For example, occasionally in astronomy, you can see more with less light. Case in point: the emergence of a giant planet in observations made by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), when astronomers found a way to block out light from the planet's parent star. The extrasolar planet, or exoplanet , in question is 51 Eridani b (51 ERI b), a gas giant with the same mass as around 11 Jupiters that orbits a star located around 97 light-years away. 51 ERI b was discovered back in 2015 by ground-based telescopes, but the planet was missing from observations of the system made by the JWST. That wasn't a failing of the JWST itself; no one is doubting the observing capabilities of the most powerful telescope humanity has ever hoisted into orbit around Earth. Instead, it was a result of starlight from the star 51 ERI A obscuring this intimidatingly massive world. The brightest planets are 100,000 times fainter than their host stars, meaning spotting them is like observing a firefly hovering around a lighthouse. Even using a tool called a coronagraph to block the star isn't enough to reveal the planet, as that doesn't stop all the starlight. The only solution to this glaring problem is a computer program to wipe out the starlight. "For the past 20 years, astronomers have tackled this problem by observing a different star and using its image as a reference," Jason Wang of Northwestern University explained in a statement . "Then, they subtract that reference image from the original observation to remove the unwanted glare to reveal faint planets that otherwise might be hidden." There is a problem with this process, however. Even the most stable telescopes "wobble." For instance, the JWST requires cryocoolers to keep its NIRCam instrument super cold, and those coolers have little motors that can cause the mirrors to vibrate. This movement, however slight, causes a scatter in starlight. The result is enough glare remaining to obscure a planet, but Wang and colleagues developed a new approach to this problem. Telescopes their more stable digital twins The new approach taken by the team is dubbed Physics-based Learning for Imaging Planets (FLIP), and it involves creating a digital "twin" of a telescope. Essentially a virtual replica that simulates how starlight travels through the telescope's mirrors and reaches its detectors. This twin is then fine-tuned to account for millions of tiny imperfections in the original telescope. The digital twin is then tweaked until it aligns with observations from the actual telescope. Astronomers can then remove the simulated glare from the original image. To assess the validity of the technique, the researchers took a second look at JWST observations of two star systems with known exoplanets, HIP 65426 and 51 Eridani , and one system, TYC 5899, with no known planets.
